items.why: Shows how Instacart is widening its categories while its DoorDash merger is under review.

items.title: Tesla Opens Sales Of Autonomous Cybercab For ‘Select’ Customers
items.summary: Tesla has opened sales of its Cybercab, which has no steering wheel or pedals, to select customers, amid a federal probe.
items.why: Autonomous-vehicle commercialisation, with regulatory risk attached.

items.title: White House Urges Easing Liability to Encourage AI Disclosure
items.summary: Officials from the Trump administration's AI task force recommended that agencies ease cyber liability policies to encourage AI companies to report critical incidents.
items.why: AI policy shift that affects lab compliance and risk.

items.title: He Was China’s Man in Panama. Then He Became a Wanted Man.
items.summary: A Chinese businessman arrived in Panama with money and power, sold a port when his luck turned, and China now wants him sent back.
items.why: Outstanding deal-and-geopolitics long read on ports and dealmaking.

items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips are behind China's most powerful AI models
items.summary: Export-restricted Nvidia chips are reportedly powering some of China's leading AI models.
items.why: Shows how leaky chip controls are, the core issue in the Nvidia scandal.

items.title: First Watch is launching a mobile-exclusive weekday menu
items.summary: First Watch is introducing a weekday menu available only through its mobile app.
items.why: A digital traffic lever from a fast-growing multi-unit breakfast chain.

items.title: Afterpay Co-Founder Molnar to Leave Dorsey’s Block at Year-End
items.summary: Afterpay co-founder Nick Molnar will leave the company and its U.S. parent, Block Inc., at the end of the year.
items.why: Fintech leadership change at Block.

items.title: Top Democrat Eyes Filibuster-Proof Budget Bill to Unlock Affordability Agenda
items.summary: The lawmaker set to lead the House Budget Committee outlines options for a filibuster-proof budget bill to force a negotiation with Trump on affordability.
items.why: Fiscal and policy outlook after the midterms.

items.title: Bessent says agencies agreed on listing Megaspeed as a national security risk
items.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a Friday interview that his department and others agreed on placing Megaspeed on a list of companies posing national security concerns.
items.why: Latest on the Megaspeed China-chip dispute inside the administration.

items.title: Protein Startups Are Selling Lots Of Snacks And Drinks. Our Sample Tasting Found Most Neither Great Nor Horrible
items.summary: A tasting review of protein-focused snacks and drinks from startups and established food brands.
items.why: A ground-level read on the crowded protein category that VCs keep funding.

items.title: Cravath Employee Is Charged With Insider Trading Using Confidential Deal Information
items.summary: Prosecutors say a Cravath employee netted $70,000 trading on confidential deal information tied to client matters including Paramount.
items.why: M&A insider-trading case touching a top deal law firm.

items.title: ElevenLabs' new app combines meeting note-taking and dictation for teams
items.summary: ElevenLabs has launched an app that pairs meeting transcription with dictation for team use.
items.why: A leading voice-AI company moves into the crowded workplace-tools market.

items.title: Blackstone’s AirTrunk Advances $11 Billion India Data Center Bet
items.summary: AirTrunk, owned by Blackstone, filed plans for two hyperscale data center campuses in southern India involving about $11 billion of investment.

items.title: Study Hard, Get a Career and Get Ahead? It’s Not What It Used to Be.
items.summary: From India to France, the implicit bargain that study and a career lead to advancement is weakening for new generations.
items.why: Big-picture economics of opportunity and labor markets.

items.title: Inside the race to make non-creepy smart glasses
items.summary: Warby Parker, Gentle Monster and HTC are positioning privacy as a product feature, while young consumers assume cameras are always on.
items.why: Consumer AI hardware meeting eyewear and fashion brands.

items.title: Nectar launches an AI agent to automate creator discovery and outreach for brands
items.summary: Nectar's new AI agent finds creators and handles outreach on behalf of brands.

items.title: China Looks to Shake Up Centuries-Old Business of Insuring Ships
items.summary: China is looking to shake up the centuries-old business of insuring ships; the newsletter also covers U.S. home sales falling to their lowest since 2010.
items.why: Markets and macro read on shipping insurance and housing.

items.title: Nvidia Crisis Spurs Scrutiny of Agency That Oversees Chip Curbs
items.summary: The US official who runs export controls had considered inviting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as a marquee name for the agency's annual conference.
items.why: Shows the coziness between the chip regulator and Nvidia.

items.title: Powerful Trump Allies Aided a Chinese Vape Operation
items.summary: Chris LaCivita and his son are helping the importer of Geek Bar capitalize on the administration's loosening of tobacco regulations.
items.why: Investigative look at a fast-growing consumer category and regulation.

items.title: Trump’s Oil Grab in Venezuela Is Testing the Country’s National Identity
items.summary: Long-held Venezuelan beliefs about sovereign control over oil are fraying as the U.S. lays claim to the country's oil reserves.

items.title: Israel's VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia's turmoil

items.title: Morgan Stanley's Shalett 'Incredibly' Bullish Despite AI Turmoil

items.title: This Permitting Overhaul Can't Come Fast Enough

items.title: Trump Signals New Strategy on Iran: A Waiting Game
items.summary: The administration appears to be moving toward a long-term economic pressure campaign on Iran, with little urgency from President Trump.

items.title: How Global Services May Be the New Protectionist Target: New Economy
items.summary: A swelling globalization wave in services threatens new challenges for developed nations and may become the next protectionist target.

items.title: Bitcoin Holds Below $70,000 as Risk-Off Mood Pressures Crypto
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August and was on track for a sixth weekly loss as rate expectations and the tech selloff sapped risk appetite.
